query: Which method can be used for oxidation resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Subjecting as‐cast AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy to stationary friction processing will refine its coarse microstructure, enabling the formation of a protective oxide scale during high‐temperature exposure and thereby enhancing oxidation resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: As‐cast equimolar AlCoCrFeNi HEA with coarse grains (~98 μm) that tend to form non‐protective spinel oxides during oxidation.
generation.intervention: Apply stationary friction processing using a WC-cylindrical tool at rotational speeds (e.g., 400 rpm and 1800 rpm) for a short duration (5 minutes) to induce severe plastic deformation.
generation.conditions: Isothermal high-temperature oxidation tests in laboratory air at temperatures of 850 °C, 950 °C, and 1050 °C for 100 hours.
generation.structural_mediator: An ultrafine-grain microstructure (reduced to ~1 μm or below) with a high density of grain boundaries and a phase transformation (from BCC/B2 to increased FCC fraction) along with an enhanced surface free energy.
generation.mechanism: The refined microstructure facilitates rapid outward diffusion of Cr and inward diffusion of oxygen, which promotes the formation of a dense, continuous protective oxide scale (predominantly Al₂O₃ and Cr₂O₃) while suppressing the formation of nonprotective spinels.
generation.predicted_outcome: Oxidation kinetics will decelerate, leading to reduced cumulative mass gain and lower parabolic rate constants for friction-processed samples compared to as-cast alloys.
generation.baseline: The as-cast HEA exhibits higher oxidation rates with a cumulative mass gain (e.g., 0.33 mg/cm² at 850 °C after 100 h) due to less-protective oxide scale formation.
generation.boundary: This outcome is expected for equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys under static dry-air conditions at 850–1050 °C; effects in other alloy systems or significantly different environments have not been established.
generation.uncertainty: While enhanced oxidation resistance is anticipated based on microstructural refinement, the quantitative improvement and long-term stability of the protective oxide scale depend on detailed processing parameters and may vary with different friction processing conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of AlCoCrFeNi HEA samples: one set as-cast and one set processed by stationary friction processing (with defined parameters). Expose both sets to isothermal oxidation in laboratory air at 850 °C, 950 °C, and 1050 °C for 100 hours in a thermogravimetric analyzer. Post-exposure, analyze the samples using SEM, TEM, and XRD to assess grain size, oxide scale composition, and mass gain.
measurements: Morphology of the oxide scale (via SEM/TEM)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If stationary friction processing does not produce a statistically significant reduction in mass gain and does not promote the formation of continuous protective oxide layers (i.e., if the friction-processed samples show oxide scales and oxidation kinetics similar to the as-cast samples), then the hypothesis will be falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Paper card. Question: How does an ultrafine-grain microstructure, obtained via stationary friction processing, affect the oxidation behavior of AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy?. System: Equimolar AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy (HEA). Processing: Stationary friction processing (SFP) using a WC-cylindrical tool (12 mm diameter) at rotational speeds of 400 rpm and 1800 rpm for 5 min duration. Test conditions: Isothermal oxidation in laboratory air at 850, 950, and 1050 °C for 100 h. Findings: Grain size refined from 98 μm (as-cast) to 1 μm (SFP_400) and 0.43 μm (SFP_1800).; Phase transformation from BCC/B2 to FCC occurred, with 38% and 55% FCC fraction for SFP_400 and SFP_1800, respectively.; Surface free energy increased by 29.8% for SFP_400 and 35.2% for SFP_1800 compared to as-cast.; Oxidation kinetics decelerated by 12–20% for SFP_400 and 38–48% for SFP_1800 compared to as-cast.; Cumulative mass gain at 850 °C after 100 h was 0.33 mg/cm² (as-cast), 0.27 mg/cm² (SFP_400), and 0.17 mg/cm² (SFP_1800).; Parabolic rate constants (k_p) at 1050 °C were 23.2 × 10⁻¹³ g²·cm⁻⁴·s⁻¹ (as-cast), 18.4 × 10⁻¹³ (SFP_400), and 8.16 × 10⁻¹³ (SFP_1800).; Processed samples formed predominantly protective
